extracted.intended_audience: academic authors and researchers (humanities, social sciences, business) considering publishing a book with Palgrave Macmillan
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers and academics on selecting a book format, understanding Palgrave Macmillan's editorial/production standards, and submitting a book idea or proposal to the publisher. Covers formats (monographs, reference works, handbooks, Pivot, textbooks), open access options, and author services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert editorial support and rigorous peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: All Palgrave Macmillan books benefit from expert editorial support and are subject to rigorous peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial support and peer review apply across Palgrave formats; this is presented as a baseline quality standard ensuring scholarly rigour and editorial input throughout the publication process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access books and chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: You can choose to publish your academic book or chapter open access, making it freely available to anyone with internet access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open access allows unrestricted online access with no reading or subscription fees; authors retain copyright and can comply with funders' open access mandates. Palgrave states open access works receive the same editorial and production process as non-open access but enjoy greater visibility and reach (on average 10× more downloads, 2.4× more citations, 10× more online mentions, and reach 61% more countries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the right book format for your publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The various publication formats vary in length, range, and depth. You can choose the format and scope that best align with your research objectives and desired impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should match format (monograph, handbook, pivot, textbook, reference work, series) to goals such as rapid impact, pedagogical use, comprehensive reference, or cutting-edge research; the publisher offers editorial help to select the appropriate format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monograph standards and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Palgrave Macmillan’s peer-reviewed monographs are known for exploring evolving, and cutting-edge research areas such as cybersecurity, mathematical finance, agricultural economics, environmental humanities, sustainability, and artificial intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monographs can be published as part of established book series. They are intended for in-depth, original research across humanities, social sciences, and business and will be discoverable via Springer Nature Link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major Reference Works: authoritative, comprehensive, and living reference model
rubrics_metrics.description: Major Reference Works are authoritative and comprehensive overviews of substantial breadth and depth on a central topic; published using an online-first Living Reference Model, continuously updated through a dynamic, peer‑reviewed publishing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features include online-first publishing (individual entries available once ready), entries citable by DOI (including updated material), collaboration with an editor-in-chief and in-house editorial team, and processing via the Meteor submission platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Palgrave Handbooks: specially commissioned, agenda-setting overviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Palgrave Handbooks are original reference works that bring together specially-commissioned chapters, cutting-edge research, and the latest review articles in their fields, providing an unparalleled overview and setting the agenda for future directions of the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handbooks are organized collections intended to map and influence a field; editorial commissioning and chapter selection are central quality mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional business and professional finance books: authoritative and accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Palgrave Macmillan’s professional business and professional finance books feature authoritative and accessible texts for business and finance professionals, from graduate employees to chief executives and managing directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These titles should balance scholarly authority with practical accessibility for practitioner and managerial audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Palgrave Pivot: concise, rapid scholarly monographs (25,000–50,000 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Palgrave Pivot combines speed with quality, offering authors a concise format of 25,000–50,000 words; longer than an article but shorter than a monograph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pivot is positioned for rapid publication on timely, topical issues and emerging areas; it reduces time-to-publication without compromising editorial standards and broadens reach beyond academia to policy and practitioner audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook standards: accessibility and rigorous review
rubrics_metrics.description: Palgrave Textbooks are accessibly written, rigorously reviewed books aimed at students taking a variety of courses across the social sciences, humanities, business, economics, finance, politics, and international studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks must be pedagogically suitable for undergraduate to postgraduate levels, provide up-to-date content, and support teaching and learning objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing in a Palgrave Macmillan book series
rubrics_metrics.description: Palgrave Macmillan book series foster in-depth and impactful scholarly dialogue; when you publish your work in a Palgrave Macmillan series alongside related research, it benefits from engaged and relevant readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series publication gives credibility and recognition, editorial input tailored to the series, and dedicated promotion to maximise visibility and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive editorial experience and global marketing & distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: When you publish with Palgrave Macmillan, you'll benefit from a supportive editorial experience and global marketing and distribution, to enable your work to achieve its full potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher offers services beyond editorial review, including marketing, promotion, and global distribution to increase impact and readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit your book idea: low‑commitment initial support
rubrics_metrics.description: If you already have an idea for a book, even in the early stages, you can fill out this form, with no obligation, to get personal support in growing it into a book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission pathway is presented as accessible and low-risk, offering personalised editorial guidance prior to formal proposal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform and workflow features for reference work entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Major Reference Works use an online-first model and the Meteor manuscript submission platform for straightforward and smooth processing; individual entries are citable by DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contributors to reference works, expect continuous updating, DOI citation for entries, and a publisher-managed online workflow to publish entries once ready.
